chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) who said:
I asked him about a child: is the funeral prayer performed for him if he dies at the age of five years? He said: 'When he understands the prayer, the funeral prayer is performed for him.'

key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: The child (specifically in the context of death and funeral rites)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: The prayer (specifically Salat al-Janazah in this context)
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: Funeral prayer is performed for him

ai.seo_question: At what age is the funeral prayer performed for a deceased child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) clarifies that the obligation of Salat al-Janazah for a child is contingent upon 'aql' (intellectual maturity) rather than a fixed chronological age, reflecting the Shia emphasis on individual capacity. This ruling distinguishes the child's status from that of an adult, linking the ritual validity to their cognitive ability to comprehend the prayer, a principle widely accepted by jurists in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* tradition.
